text: The query works, but right now anyone with access to Snowflake could run it. This lesson sets up the one role this project actually needs — a read-only analyst role, with exactly enough access to do its job.
First, create the role. On its own, a role does absolutely nothing — it's an empty container with zero privileges until you grant it something.

Next, the chain of USAGE grants: on the warehouse, on the database, and on the schema. A role needs permission at every single level between logging in and reading an object's data. Miss any one link, and the whole chain breaks, no matter what you grant at the end.

Notice what's deliberately not granted yet. There's no SELECT on anything here — because the one object this role actually needs to read, the summary view, doesn't exist until next lesson. The infrastructure access is ready now; the object-specific grant waits until the object is real. And notice what never gets granted at all: SELECT on the raw tickets table. This role doesn't need raw rows, so it never gets them.

Last, the role gets assigned to an actual person — granted to the user who'll open the Power BI report, not to the admin role you've been building everything with so far. That separation is the whole point: the analyst inherits exactly this project's access, nothing more.
The role exists, the infrastructure access is granted. Next lesson, we create the actual view this role is waiting to read — and hand it the one SELECT grant it's still missing.
